Kevin Trudeau lived in a 900 square foot apartment with a sheet covering the window because he was broke.

Every day he pictured himself in a mansion — not wanting it, actually feeling like he already lived there.

The apartment eventually became multiple mansions worth millions. The part that mattered, he says: his internal state never changed. Same feeling in 900 square feet as in the mansion, in a beat-up car as in a Rolls-Royce.

That's the piece most people skip.

Herb Cohen walked into his negotiation seminar smoking a cigar and said the secret of life in five words: care, but not that much.

Kevin Trudeau says he heard the same lesson inside The Brotherhood, over and over — you care too much, release, let go.

Wanting something desperately is exactly what blocks it. The people who actually get what they want have released their grip on needing it.
